# Meetings keep their notes with the work

When a meeting app writes a note into Imprimatur, that note lands on the task it was actually about. You get a clear list of your meetings, grouped by month, with decisions and to-dos pulled out so you can see what was agreed without rereading the whole note.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)
- [Words used here](#words-used-here)

## What it does for you

- Shows your meetings for the current project, grouped by month, with real meeting names instead of generic titles.
- Lets you open a meeting to see decisions and to-dos in two columns, your own items listed first.
- Links each meeting back to the task it was about, so the agreement sits next to the work.
- Shows the meeting's raw transcript alongside its note, in case the note missed something that was actually said.
- Lets you search for a phrase from the conversation even if it only appears in the transcript, not the note.

## How it works

1. A meeting app sends the note after a meeting ends.
2. Imprimatur attaches it to the task the meeting was about, or to a general "Meetings" task if it wasn't about one specific piece of work.
3. Decisions and to-dos from the note are pulled out and shown as their own items, linked to that meeting.
4. You see the meeting in your project's Meetings list, with its date, name, a short summary, and counts of decisions and your open to-dos.
5. Opening the meeting shows the decisions, to-dos, the task it belongs to, the full note, and the transcript underneath.

## Good to know

- The Meetings list only shows meetings from the project you currently have open, even if you've set a wider "every project" view elsewhere.
- If a meeting is rewritten and sent again, it updates the same entry rather than creating a duplicate.
- If a meeting note is withdrawn, it and everything pulled from it disappear together.

## Words used here

- repo: the project or codebase a task and its meetings belong to.
- task: a piece of work, tracked by its ticket number, that a meeting can be linked to.
- to-do: an action item from a meeting, with the person who took it on.
